title: Chiral Weyl--Kondo semimetal and circular photogalvanic effect in a prototype Kondo lattice system
authors: Yuan Fang, Kuan-Sen Lin, Mounica Mahankali, Arushi, Kevin Allen, Sanu Mishra, Emilia Morosan, Qimiao Si
abstract: Chiral Weyl--Kondo semimetals (cWKSM) provide a setting in which chiral Weyl quasiparticles emerge in the immediate vicinity of the Fermi energy from a Kondo-driven reconstruction of the strongly correlated electronic states in chiral heavy fermion systems (K.-S. Lin et al., arXiv:2602.22185). A defining characteristic of this strongly correlated topological state is the Kramers chiral Weyl fermions in the low-energy quasiparticle states. Recently, experiments in CeGaGe have emerged as a concrete realization of the proposed effect (Arushi et al., preprint). Motivated by these findings, here we go beyond the materials-specific effects by constructing a prototype Kondo lattice model; it incorporates only the essential couplings that respect the associated tetragonal crystalline symmetries. This simplification allows us to robustly demonstrate the symmetry-enforced Kramers Weyl fermions and related topological nodal states in the spectrum of heavy quasiparticles. Furthermore, the simplification provides a tractable setting to determine the salient features in the system's nonlinear optical response, the circular photogalvanic effect, in chiral Weyl--Kondo semimetals. Both analytical and numerical calculations identify sharp peaks in the frequency domain as signatures of the Kondo-driven chiral Weyl nodes; the sharpness of the spectrum reflects the resonant nature of the underlying strongly correlated electronic excitations. Thus, cWKSM provides a unique setting to spectroscopically identify topological fermions that are induced by strong electron correlations. As such, our results are expected to bring about much needed new insights into the understanding of strongly correlated gapless topological matter.
summary: This work develops a theoretical model for chiral Weyl-Kondo semimetals, demonstrating how strong electron correlations induce topological Weyl fermions. By calculating the Circular Photogalvanic Effect, the authors show that these Kondo-driven topological nodes leave a unique, sharp resonance signature in the optical response spectrum. This provides a spectroscopic pathway to identify strongly correlated topological matter.
main_problem: The paper aims to understand the emergence and spectroscopic identification of topological fermions, specifically chiral Weyl quasiparticles, in strongly correlated systems driven by Kondo interactions.
main_result: The model robustly demonstrates symmetry-enforced Kramers Weyl fermions, and these topological nodes manifest as sharp, resonance-like peaks in the Circular Photogalvanic Effect (CPGE) frequency spectrum.
method: The study employs a prototype Kondo lattice model solved using the infinite-U limit and the parton method, followed by calculating the nonlinear optical response (CPGE) using Green's function techniques.
model_or_system: The system is a chiral Weyl-Kondo semimetal (cWKSM) modeled by a Kondo lattice Hamiltonian incorporating conduction and localized f-electron states, respecting tetragonal crystalline symmetries.
key_observables: Chiral Weyl nodes, Kramers–Weyl points, and the Circular Photogalvanic Effect (CPGE) spectrum ($ eta$ vs $\omega$).
important_parameters: Strong correlation regime ($U \gg$ bandwidth), Kondo temperature ($T_K$), and the frequency ($\omega$) relative to the Kondo resonance.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on constructing a prototype model with essential couplings and utilizes the saddle-point approximation in the infinite-U limit.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic of Weyl/anti-Weyl points, the crystal structure, the quasiparticle band dispersion, and the calculated CPGE response showing characteristic resonance peaks.
paper_structure: The paper develops the model Hamiltonian, analyzes the symmetry-enforced topological nodes (Weyl/Kramers points), and then calculates the CPGE response, demonstrating how Kondo correlations modify the expected optical signature.
why_interesting: The connection between strong electronic correlations (Kondo physics) and topological responses (Weyl nodes) is highly relevant to understanding exotic quantum materials and their optical properties.
